name: fir chlis

attributes.attribute: Gaelic term formed from chlis, quick and nimble
sometimes translated as the merry dancers
takes the article na in Gaelic usage

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Fir chlis is a figure of Scottish folklore. Known as the nimble man, he stood for the northern lights, called the aurora borealis. He appears in the folklore of Scotland. MacKillop glosses the name in Scottish Gaelic from chlis, meaning quick, lively, or nimble. The term names the aurora borealis in Gaelic folklore, and writers sometimes render it as the merry dancers. In Gaelic usage the plural term takes the definite article na before it. Gaelic speakers therefore say na fir chlis when they name the lights. The term serves as a named spirit of the lights. It also stands as the everyday Gaelic label for the display itself.

okr.objective: fir chlis names the northern lights in Scottish Gaelic folklore as the nimble man or merry dancers.
